column2:
Risks to community health and safety due to
the transport, storage, and use and/or
disposal of materials such as explosives, fuel
and other chemicals during operation
column3:
• No explosives will be used
• Mandatory use of appropriate PPE,
Reagents and chemicals used in testing
protocols, while complex, are in pure
solution following the guidelines and
requirements of WHO
• Temporary storage will refer to WHO
specific guidelines
• Fuel and other chemicals will be kept
appropriately designed storage area

column2:
Community safety risks due to both
accidental and natural causes, especially
where the structural elements or components
of the project are accessible to members of
the affected community or where their failure
could result in injury to the community
throughout project operation and
decommissioning
column3:
• Appropriate design features to meet
national and international standards will
be included, and measures/plans and
procedures will be implemented to
minimize risks.
• Unauthorized public access to the
construction sites and laboratories will be
prohibited.
• Environmental audit and risk assessment
will be conducted during implementation.
• Regular monitoring will be done under
direct management of a professional
Occupational Health & Safety Officer.

column2:
Community health and safety risks due to
generation of solid and hazardous waste, and
its transportation to designated disposal site
column3:
• Trained and qualified waste transport
company will be employed and the same
will be required to comply with WHO
certified COVID-19 contamination control
guidelines for handling waste including
hazardous waste
• General municipal waste and hazardous
wastes to be screened at source,
separated and disposed temporarily in the
bin at two different designated locations
as nonhazardous designated place, and
hazardous materials designated places
for time-bound disposals
• Non-hazardous will be disposed to
municipality owned disposal site.
• Generation of solid waste will comply with
relevant provisions in the City Corporation
Act 2009 on waste removal, collection and
management
• Medical waste management will comply
with the requirements of WHO proposed
